info.title: Super Artifacts REST API
info.description: Publish, read and share artifacts, and read and write their data, with an account key. Each operation is one MCP tool call: the same limits, errors and permissions. Errors are `{error: {code, message}}`; `code` is stable.

get.summary: Who this key publishes as
get.description: Who this key publishes as: the workspace `handle`, `email`, `agent` name and `scope` (the artifacts it may change: its own, and those it is named Editor on), plus `liveRooms` where live rooms run (the limit and who holds one). Useful to confirm where a publish lands, or why an artifact answers `not_found`; no other tool needs it.

200.description: Who this key publishes as

get.summary: How the operations fit together
get.description: Plain-text notes for when it is unclear which tool, data store or argument shape does a job. Topics: `tools` (a line per tool), `data` (which store a page needs and how the page writes to it), `templates` (finding, building from, drafting, releasing), `collections` (content models and field types), `projects` (creating, ordering, sharing, rules), `batch` (what each tool takes in one call). Without `topic`: the full topic list, which names two more reached from results. Answers `{topic, text}`; not needed when a tool’s own description answers the question.

200.description: How the operations fit together

get.summary: List account webhook endpoints
get.description: Manage this account’s webhook endpoints. create and rotate return the signing secret once; delete permanently removes an endpoint and its delivery history. Mutations require write scope. agent: "me" selects the calling key’s agent (no_agent if absent); a handle must be owned. messages returns the newest 100, optionally filtered by endpoint id and sinceMinutes (1–43200). Declare artifact triggers through super_publish.

get.summary: List your artifacts, newest first
get.description: Without `artifact`: your artifacts, newest first, with URLs and `live`. With `artifact`: its versions, which is published, their paths, and `declaration` (the published policy). Add `path` or `version` to read that file as text (default: published index.html); non-text or over 300,000 bytes: refused. `open: true` (with `artifact`, optional `version`) returns `url` and `expiresAt`: load `url` to see the artifact as a viewer, private included, for 10 minutes; visibility is unchanged, the URL opens only that artifact, 60/key/hour (`rate_limited`). Changing what an artifact serves, or who can open it, is super_artifact_set.

200.description: List your artifacts, newest first

post.summary: Publish an artifact, or a new version of one
post.description: Publish a page at a stable URL; the same slug adds a new version, which the URL serves at once. Earlier versions stay and can be served again; nothing that existed before the call is deleted. Always give the person the url from the result, even on updates. Send `html`, or `values` for a template that carries a runtime, not both. Without `policy` a form, input or saved state stores nothing; CMS rows a page edits go in `policy.collections`. When retained storage is full it refuses with `plan_limit` and deletes nothing. A template becomes everybody’s through a release, not a publish.

slug.description: Kebab-case, 3–63 chars, under your key’s handle: it updates one there you are Editor on. Another workspace’s artifact: publish from its dashboard.

prompt.description: Optional: the request it answers, on its card.

values.description: Filled slots for `template`'s runtime, by slot name; `json` slots are schema-checked.

instances.description: Instead of `slug`/`values`: several pages of one `template`.

template.description: The template built from (provenance); required with `values` or `instances`.

kind.description: Default `page`. `dashboard` labels a page of mostly live data.

collection.description: Gallery grouping label, not a content collection.

visibility.description: From version 1. Default: the workspace default; public is set after.

policy.description: Data policy v1. Visitors submit to a sheet (perUser single, upsert, a field per question), a log (many, append-only) or a shared doc (shared, key). CMS rows: `collections`. See super_help data.

triggers.description: Declared agent triggers: key, prompt, optional label, on, who, agent, input, when, once. At most 8 and 12 KiB; omitted on redeploy keeps the previous set.

continues.description: With `values`: the dataset key this one succeeds.

uploads.description: uploadId from super_upload; its files ship with the page.

valuesFile.description: With `uploads`: the staged JSON file to read `values` from.

files.description: With `html`: small assets. ≤200, 5 MiB each, 10 MiB total, decoded.

sha256.description: Hex digest of the decoded bytes.

200.description: Publish an artifact, or a new version of one

patch.summary: Change visibility, gallery label, live phase or submission email
patch.description: Change one artifact. `version` serves an existing version (a pointer move; nothing rebuilt or deleted). `live` turns its live room on or off; off disconnects every visitor, and Free has one room at a time. `triggersEnabled` is the owner’s kill switch for declared triggers (default on). `notifyOnSubmission` emails you for each new data submission (default off; edits send nothing; no answers in the mail). `phase` sets the live room’s phase. `visibility` widens or narrows who can open it; narrowing voids every viewer grant already issued, so each viewer is checked again. `collection` sets its gallery grouping label. `delete` removes the artifact with every version, share link and response, permanently; it needs `confirm: true` and goes alone. Fields apply in that order, and a refusal part-way names the ones already `applied`. Publishing a new version is super_publish.

visibility.description: private: Restricted (default). organization: anyone at the workspace. public: anyone with the link.

collection.description: Gallery grouping label, ≤ 60 chars. Empty clears it.

phase.description: The name a stream’s `revealAt` waits for; from then on that stream reads as public.

200.description: Change visibility, gallery label, live phase or submission email

post.summary: Stage big files for a publish; PUT each to its URL
post.description: Stage images, video or big files for a publish without sending their bytes in a call. Declare each file’s `path` and exact `bytes`; the result carries an `uploadId` and one `url` per file. PUT each file to its URL (`curl -T`, no credentials), then super_publish with `uploads`. Not index.html: that is `html`; small assets can ride inline as the publish’s `files`. Same limits as `files`; a staged set expires after 30 minutes, and at most 5 wait unpublished at once.

200.description: Stage big files for a publish; PUT each to its URL

get.summary: Rows visitors submitted to one artifact, newest first
get.description: The rows visitors submitted to your artifacts, newest first, with each version's field schema; paged by `cursor`. Address exactly one: `artifact`; `dataset` (a catalog key; one shared by several artifacts is `ambiguous_dataset`); or `collection`, the gallery grouping label set at publish, not a content collection (≤20 artifacts over one window, kept per artifact, no `filter`). Entries of a content collection are super_entries; totals and averages are a query, not a read.

parameters.name: filter
parameters.description: ANDed 'field op value' clauses: 'reps >= 5', 'day in mon,tue', 'note is set'. Ops: = != > >= < <= contains in, is set, is unset. System: _version _at _status _visitor.

parameters.name: since
parameters.description: ISO-8601 instant or window (7d, 24h). Or a version (v2) when addressing one artifact.

200.description: Rows visitors submitted to one artifact, newest first

post.summary: Write rows into an artifact you may edit
post.description: Write rows into an artifact this key may edit, through the validation and stream rules a page write gets; each row is attributed "<agent> (agent)". `rows` creates in `stream`. `ops` [{op: create|replace|delete, id, row, stream}] replaces or deletes only rows this agent wrote (writes: upsert); a deleted row cannot be restored by any tool. ≤50 a call; `atomic`: all or none, otherwise a partial batch answers `complete: false`. Visitor rows are never changed here; entries of a content collection are super_entries.

post.summary: Aggregate what was collected: numbers, never rows
post.description: Numbers over what was collected, never rows (rows are super_data). Aggregate `measures` across the datasets in `scope`; datasets combine on the same measure in one base unit, results in the declared `unit`. Names come from the catalog; an unknown one errors with near misses. The answer has one row per `group_by` key (or one row) with a column per measure and `compute`, the datasets used and any skipped, and `truncated` when `limit` cut it. Or send `distributions` for one artifact: counts, per-version rates and per-field distributions (free text: answer rate and length only). A call with neither is `invalid_query`.

scope.description: The union of the forms given.

measures.description: Catalog measure names, not field names.

compute.description: Derived columns, in order; operands name a measure or an earlier `as`.

filter.description: ANDed 'field op value' clauses: 'reps >= 5', 'day in mon,tue', 'note is set'. Ops: = != > >= < <= in. Catalog fields only.

group_by.description: One of dataset, day, week, month, visitor, or "field:{name}".

distributions.description: One artifact's per-field distributions instead of a scoped query.

group_by.description: A choice, boolean or integer field.

200.description: Aggregate what was collected: numbers, never rows

get.summary: The data catalog: datasets and content collections, or a comparison
get.description: The data catalog, without rows. Read (the default): `datasets` your artifacts declared, with fields, units, measures and `since`/`deprecated` versions, and this workspace's content `collections`, with fields, rules and entry counts. `compare` (alone): two to ten artifacts' newest fields side by side, every type, unit and measure conflict named. `define` creates a content collection, or replaces the one with that `key` outright, name, display field and every field; a field left out is gone from the model, and a collection an artifact declared is refused with `conflict`. Refusals name field, rule and fix. Rows an artifact collected are super_data.

parameters.name: compare
parameters.description: Alone: 2+ ids or slugs; their fields side by side, conflicts named.

parameters.name: workspace
parameters.description: Workspace handle. Omit for your own.

post.summary: Call an approved API with a stored secret you cannot read (workspace keys)
post.description: Make one HTTPS request with a `pii: secret` value from a content collection entry. The platform puts the value into one header and calls the one host a person approved; you get status, headers and body, scrubbed of it. You never see it, in input or result; a response echoing it is withheld whole (`secret_echoed`). A first request for a field and host answers `approval_required` with `approvalUrl`: give the person that link, then repeat the request once they approve. Grants expire, cap uses and can be revoked; every use is logged. The person types the secret into its dashboard entry; super_entries writes one only if they insist on pasting it.

parameters.name: collection
parameters.description: Content collection key (a content model), not a gallery label.

parameters.name: field
parameters.description: The `pii: secret` field whose value is sent.

url.description: https only; its host must be the approved one. Redirects are returned, never followed.

headers.description: Sent as given, except host, authorization, cookie, proxy-* and the grant’s own header.

scheme.description: Prefix before the value, e.g. "Bearer ". May be empty.

header.description: Where the value goes; asked for when no grant exists. The approved grant’s header wins.

200.description: Call an approved API with a stored secret you cannot read (workspace keys)

get.summary: Find, rank or list templates
get.description: With `request`: rank installed templates by content similarity; matches carry `band` (high: build from it; possible: judge it), `why` and unscored stats. `scope: marketplace`: released public templates, ranked by `request` or else the top by `sort`; `sort`, `limit` and the facets apply only here. Neither: the installed list. `slug`: one template in full, with its `installPrompt`; `history`: its changelog; `feedback`: its artifacts' comments as themes. `mine`: your published templates, with counts. Reading only: installing, rating and rolling back are super_template_action.

parameters.description: What the person asked for, in their words.

parameters.name: cost
parameters.description: fill: you send a document; write: you write the page; build: page and policy.

parameters.name: tier
parameters.description: Marketplace trust tier: Official, Verified or Community.

post.summary: Create or revise a template draft
post.description: Write a template draft only you can publish from. Without `expectedVersion` it creates (refused if the slug exists); with it, it revises the head (refused if the head moved past it), and a revision that changes nothing cuts no version. A `json` slot needs `schema`. Runtime `files` (≤512 KiB decoded) need a `json` slot and an index.html with one `<script id="sa-template-values" type="application/json">`. Others build from it only once super_release_template releases it; a revision never changes a released version.

jobs.description: What a person hires it for; the first is primary. Create default: from `kind`.

useCases.description: Things to build from it; the build prompt draws on them.

installArchetype.description: After install: `scenarios` (default) offers three builds; `explainer` builds one from the sample; `interview` asks three questions first.

installAfter.description: Your note, appended to the build prompt as a suggestion.

samplePublic.description: The sample may appear on the public listing page.

category.description: Deprecated; read as `jobs` when `jobs` is absent.

slots.description: The fill schema, an array: [{"name": "headline", "type": "text", "required": true, "max": 120}].

guidance.description: Optional notes for whoever fills it.

prompt.description: A prompt a person copies to ask for one.

demo.description: Slug of your artifact to link as the demo (linked once public). "" clears it.

files.description: Runtime files, `index.html` required. Omitting them on a revision drops the runtime from that new draft version only.

text.description: UTF-8 text, base64-ed for you. Send `text` or `content`.

content.description: Base64 of the bytes, for binaries.

companions.description: Extra artifacts each publish makes at {slug}-{role}, same values (e.g. a stage for a host). Bind the primary with `source: {artifact: "@primary", streams}`. Released: add, never remove.

slots.description: Slot names whose values this part gets. Default all.

expectedVersion.description: The version you revised. Present: revise. Absent: create.

changeNote.description: Revisions: one line on why, for the changelog.

post.summary: Install, uninstall, rate, report, roll back or request verification
post.description: Act on one template; nothing here deletes a template, a version or a built artifact. `install`/`uninstall`: this workspace's installed set (uninstall removes only the install; built artifacts keep working); `install` returns its build prompt as `nextStep`. `rate`: the person's 1–5 `stars` on an installed template not yours (`cannot_rate_own`, `not_installed`, `rate_limited`); counts once this workspace built from it. `report`: `kind` and a `reason` (≤1000 chars) for a moderator; one per account; enough reports hide it. `rollback`: restore `version` as a new version, unless the runtime changed. `request_verification`: a moderator checks your released `version`; 3 per 30 days. post.summary: Release one version of your template
post.description: Release one version of your template so others can build from it, live at once to the reach `visibility` sets; the result names its trust `tier` (Official, Verified or Community). Forward only (`release_moves_backwards`): earlier versions stay, and nothing is deleted. A private demo needs `demoConsent: true`. A runtime, prompt, parts or data change leaves a Verified badge behind. Public: account 7 days old (`publisher_too_new`), 10/day, 3/template/hour (`rate_limited`), 20 templates (`too_many_templates`), no tier words (`reserved_wording`), no credential (`secret_in_template`), paid plan (`plan_required`). Writing the draft is super_template_save.

get.summary: Your projects
get.description: A project is an ordered set of your artifacts shown one at a time at /s/{slug}, with its own audience and share list. No `project`: `title` creates one (seeded from `artifacts`), else list yours. With `project`: add `artifacts`, `remove` one, `title` renames, set `visibility`, `order`/`move` reorder, a `rule` adds matches as they are published, or read it. `delete` with `confirm: true` removes the project, its order and its share list permanently; its artifacts stay. get.summary: An artifact's signature requests, newest first
get.description: Ask named people to sign one published version of an artifact, and follow the request. `request` with `artifact`, `signers` [{name, email, party?}] (≤10) and an optional `message` (≤500 characters) emails each signer a private link; the version must be one file of at most 2 MiB, and it is kept while the request is open and for good once it completes. `status` with `request` (one) or `artifact` (all, newest first). `withdraw` closes an open request. `remind` emails `signer` the link again, three times at most, a day apart. Only each signer can sign, in a browser, after a code sent to their address: an agent cannot.
